cim: USI receives $8.5 million artificial intelligence grant through Lilly Endowment
cim_eredeti: USI receives $8.5 million artificial intelligence grant through Lilly Endowment
szoveg_eredeti:
The three-year grant will support a coordinated University initiative focused on preparing USI graduates to leverage AI responsibly.

The University of Southern Indiana has received an $8.5 million grant from Lilly Endowment Inc. through its Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education (AIHE) initiative. USI will use the grant funding to prepare students, faculty and staff to thrive in a world increasingly shaped by artificial intelligence.

The three-year grant will support a coordinated University initiative focused on preparing USI graduates to leverage AI responsibly and ethically and make positive contributions to their communities. USI will focus on upskilling staff and 350+ full-time faculty to drive transformation in its 130 areas of study, and to support services that ensure students are equipped to succeed in and support an emerging AI workforce.

USI will develop multiple curricular, co-curricular and experiential pathways for students to build general and discipline-specific AI fluency, while also strengthening faculty and staff AI capacity, AI infrastructure, student support and academic operations.

“This investment gives USI an extraordinary opportunity to prepare our students not simply to use AI, but to understand how and when to use it responsibly and effectively within their disciplines and future careers,” said Dr. Shelly Blunt, Provost. “It will also give our faculty and staff the time, resources and support needed to thoughtfully examine what AI means for teaching, learning and student success while keeping critical thinking, human judgment, creativity and ethical decision-making at the center of a USI education.”

The work builds on a December 2025 Phase 1 planning grant from Lilly Endowment Inc. that helped the University assess its most compelling needs regarding AI, consider the most promising ideas to help address them and prepare an implementation grant proposal.

USI is among 35 Indiana colleges and universities receiving implementation grants through Lilly Endowment Inc.’s AIHE initiative. The grants, ranging from $2.5 million to $25 million, total nearly $292 million and are based on student enrollment at each institution. The Endowment has allocated $500 million for the initiative, including planning grants, implementation grants and large-scale collaborative grants.

During the planning phase, USI assessed regional workforce needs, AI topics in the curriculum and AI use in instruction while providing professional development opportunities for faculty and staff. The findings reinforced the need for both foundational AI literacy and field- and discipline-specific skills.

A USI survey of regional employers found 73% of respondents use AI for work either daily or a few times per week. Employers identified basic AI literacy, AI-assisted communication and ethical and legal use of AI among skills expected of new hires across work roles. An analysis of more than 8,100 Indiana AI-related job postings also found the state’s AI-related job market is broad and weighted heavily toward AI fluency and integration rather than AI specialization.

The grant will support eight interconnected projects, including:

AI Fluency Framework and Guidelines: USI will establish working groups to define AI fluency and develop cohesive, values-driven principles, policies and frameworks that guide ethical and responsible AI use.

Prepare Students with AI Fluency: USI will build multiple curricular, co-curricular and experiential pathways for students to develop general and discipline-specific AI fluency through course and program redesign, general education review, student innovation awards, online training and career preparation.

Develop Faculty and Staff AI Fluency: USI will strengthen faculty and staff AI capacity through professional development, communities of practice, showcases, self-paced training, discipline-specific learning funds and protected time and compensation for deeper AI-related curriculum and program improvement.

Leveraging AI in Student Academic Support: USI will assess student support gaps and deploy appropriate market-available or custom AI tools to strengthen academic and career services to improve students’ college transition, progress, graduation and work experiences.

Leveraging AI to Improve Academic Operational Effectiveness and Efficiency: USI will leverage AI tools to streamline and improve academic operations, understanding that speeding core processes enables better facilitation of student success.

Enhancing AI Infrastructure: USI recognizes that investment is needed in AI infrastructure to facilitate each of the other projects. This project will support campus-wide licenses for AI tools and infrastructure.

Community Engagement and Communications: USI will ensure continued dialogue with community stakeholders on AI issues, while also working to positively influence broader narratives around USI’s AI efforts.

Management and Evaluation: USI will ensure projects run smoothly, produce the proposed outcomes and satisfy the objectives. This also includes project evaluation and facilitation of grant reporting.

To learn more about USI's 130+ areas of study, visit USI.edu/apply.

Lilly Endowment Inc. is an Indianapolis-based private foundation created in 1937 by J.K. Lilly and his sons, Eli and J.K. Jr., through gifts of stock in their pharmaceutical business, Eli Lilly and Company. While those gifts remain the financial bedrock of the Endowment, the Endowment is a separate entity from the company, with a distinct governing board, staff and location.
